units: Ḥull. 17ᵇ, quot. s. v. טוּפְרָא) to turn the slaughtering knife on all sides, to examine.
<cite ref="Eruvin 63a:2">Erub. 63ᵃ</cite> <he>רבינא סַר סכינא וכ׳</he> R. examined the slaughterer’s knife (assumed the rabbinical function of superintending the slaughtering) in Babylonia.
<cite ref="Chullin 18a:3">Ḥull. 18ᵃ</cite> <he>דלא סר וכ׳</he> who failed to examine his knife before an authorised scholar.

senses.gloss: to go around, visit, superintend, esp. ס׳ ניכסיה (or ארעיה) to superintend one’s estate, examine, watch laborers &c.—Part. סָיֵיר. Ib. 105ᵃ מאן דסייר ניכסיה וכ׳ (Ar. סָאֵיר) he who goes around examining his property every day. Ib. וכ׳ אבא הוה ס׳ … ואנא לא סָיִירְנָא my father used to examine his estate twice a day, but I do it only once a day.

units: <cite ref="Bava Metzia 76b">B. Mets. 76ᵇ</cite>, sq. [read:] <he>סַיְּירָהּ לארעיה וכ׳</he> (v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note) he visited his fields &c.
<cite ref="Gittin 38b">Gitt. 38ᵇ</cite> <he>דמְסַיְּירֵי וכ׳</he> Rashi (ed. <he>דסָיְירֵי</he>) those who examine their property on the Sabbath; a. e.—V. <cite ref="O01293"><he>סְעַר</he> I</cite>.
